content.text:
VERDICT: LGTM

The future-date guard is placed exactly where the effective registration date is derived, as a natural third case alongside the pre-existing inline handling of the supplied `registrationDate` (null → default to today; future → reject; otherwise use as-is). It reads coherently as a single `if / else if` over the supplied value.

It matches how this controller already does field validation — a `ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, ...)` thrown from the request-handling flow, consistent with `normalizeTelephone`, `normalizeEmail`, `normalizeAddress`, and `validatePostcode`. It introduces no duplication, adds nothing to any shared/util class, and doesn't turn `addOwner` into a catch-all beyond what was already there. The registration-date block is the one concern this class already handles inline (the null-default and `rollToBusinessDay` call live right here), so extending that same block with the guard is the natural home for it rather than a separate helper. A maintainer of this file would find the placement unsurprising.
